floor.appliesTo: Full-time basic monthly salary, Singapore, 5-day week
floor.short: Below about S$2,500 basic a month, a role gets much harder to fill locally.
floor.long: This is not a rule, it is what we see. You can hire below it, but expect to wait a lot longer and to lose people to the employer up the road. Everyone is comparing. For hands-on roles on a 5-day week, S$2,500 is roughly where the market starts now.
floor.exemptNote: The S$2,500 guide is about basic pay where the basic is the whole package. Plenty of hands-on roles run a lower basic with overtime and incentives on top, and there you judge the gross instead. Where we know both, we show both.

operative.label: Hands-on roles
operative.note: Hands-on roles do not really have a junior-to-senior ladder, but they do have two numbers that matter. The basic is what you commit to. The gross is what the person takes home once overtime, incentives and allowances land, and it is the number they compare against the employer up the road. Supervisor and team leader roles sit separately, because that is more responsibility rather than the same job for longer.

professional.label: Professional & executive roles
professional.note: Banded by experience, because that is how employers brief us.

scope.label: Priced by scope

sub.Typical range: driven by how complex the work is

scope.note: These roles are not really banded by years served. What moves the number is how much the job actually carries. Tell us the duties and we will tell you where it lands.

sectors.name: Engineering

roles.name: Engineering Assistant / Technician
roles.scope: Engineering assistant, technician, maintenance technician. ITE-level technical work.
roles.basicNote: S$2,750 is where technical entry pay has settled, and below S$2,500 you will struggle for quality candidates. Not much rides on allowances here, it depends whether the role is shift or non-shift.

roles.name: Engineer
roles.scope: Mechanical, electrical, design, process, site, project, civil and structural, QA and QC.
roles.basicNote: The discipline matters less than you would think. What moves the number is how technical the work is and how much the role is accountable for. A complex, technical brief starts higher than a straightforward one with the same job title.

Typical range.note: complexity and responsibility decide where in the range

roles.name: Senior Engineer
roles.scope: Senior mechanical, senior design, lead engineer and equivalent.
roles.basicNote: Years of experience get you into this range, but they do not set the number. The industry and the company do, and the same senior title pays very differently across the two.

Typical range.note: industry and company move this as much as years do

sectors.note: Priced by level, not by discipline. There are more engineering job titles than anyone can usefully list, and two roles with the same title can sit a thousand dollars apart. What actually decides the number is how technical the work is and how much the role carries. Tell us the duties and we will place it for you. ITE-level technical roles sit in the first band below; a local diploma engineering hire starts at S$3,000 and above.

roles.aboveNote: Above this you are into team leader or assistant supervisor, which is more responsibility rather than a wider job scope. We list that separately.

floor.appliesTo: Basic monthly salary, Singapore production and operator roles
floor.short: In manufacturing the basic is only half the story. Aim for a gross around S$3,000.
floor.long: Production and operator pay runs a lower basic than most sectors, with overtime and incentives doing a lot of the work. Around S$1,800 basic is the practical minimum anyone will take. Start the basic at S$2,000 and you are in the normal range; S$2,200 to S$2,500 and you attract noticeably better production staff. But the number people actually judge is the gross, and around S$3,000 a month is what tends to win them. Fewer people want to chase overtime these days, so a package that only works with heavy OT is a harder sell.

sectors.note: Pay is only half of it here. How straightforward the scope is moves the number as much as the band does, and at the lower end of the basic range the pool is smaller and the search takes longer. Tell us the scope and we will tell you what it will actually take to fill.

sectors.name: Healthcare

roles.name: Registered Nurse
roles.basicNote: These bands are what the market is paying. A staff nurse can start lower, around S$2,730 base, but base is not what a nurse compares and it is not what closes a hire. Shift and department allowances sit on top of all of these.

roles.name: Enrolled Nurse
roles.basicNote: Base only, and base is the problem here. S$2,050 will not attract anyone in this market. A clinic assistant, front desk and helping the doctor, already starts above S$2,500 and runs to about S$3,000. A nurse carries far more than that. Budget a starting gross of about S$3,000 once shift and department allowances are in, or expect a long search.

roles.name: Clinic Assistant
roles.scope: Front desk plus assisting the doctor, GP or dental.
roles.basicNote: Starts above S$2,500 and the going rate is around S$3,000. We recently placed one at S$2,800 basic with no allowances on top, on a 5-day 44-hour week with shifts but no midnight shift. Hiring is not the hard part here, keeping someone is: below this range people move on.

Basic.note: around S$3,000 is the going rate
Basic.verifiedNote: JTE, Nov 2026, against placements we closed.

roles.name: Care / Support Staff
roles.scope: Healthcare assistant and care staff. Certification needed, but easier to get than nursing.
roles.basicNote: Lower than nursing because the certification is easier to get, but do not read that as cheap. Even at S$2,500 this is a difficult hire now, so S$2,500 is where we would start rather than where we would aim. Allowances only really come in when the job requires going out to clients, so for most of these the basic is close to what the person takes home.

Basic.note: start at the floor and expect a slow search

roles.name: Pharmacy
roles.basicNote: This band covers pharmacy roles broadly, and at the lower end it is assistant and technician work. S$2,500 is the floor we would work to. A registered pharmacist starts materially higher, from about S$3,850. Ask us which one you are hiring.

floor.appliesTo: Base monthly salary, Singapore community care and support roles
floor.short: Care roles run on bands, not one rate. A care staff role starts around S$2,480.
floor.long: Community care pay sits on salary bands rather than one market rate. The entry level, a health attendant, starts at S$1,800. A healthcare assistant or care staff role starts at about S$2,480 and runs to roughly S$3,300 as people progress. Those are base figures, so overtime, shift and department allowances sit on top. Nursing is the one to watch. Base bands are real, but they are not what a nurse compares and not what closes a hire. For scale: a clinic assistant already starts above S$2,500, and we recently placed one at S$2,800 basic with no allowances at all. A nurse carries far more responsibility than that, so budget a starting gross of about S$3,000 at the least, allowances included, or the role will sit open. Nursing is a hard hire here and pay has moved up accordingly.

sectors.note: Pay here depends more on which band a role sits in than on years served. If you tell us the duties and the level of supervision, we can tell you the band it lands in and what it will take to fill.

roles.name: Administrative
roles.basicNote: Complexity drives this one, not years. Simple data entry sits near the bottom of the range, a role that actually runs things sits near the top.

Typical range.note: data entry at the low end, full office support at the top

roles.name: Secretary
roles.basicNote: A different job from administrative support, not a promotion from it. The top of this range is for someone supporting senior leadership.

Typical range.note: scales with who you are supporting and what you are trusted with
